edges.population: adults exposed to chronic pyridoxine supplements, especially prolonged doses above standard replacement ranges
edges.mechanism: Excess pyridoxine preferentially injures sensory neurons, likely through disruption of pyridoxal kinase-dependent pathways and downstream sensory-neuron dysfunction, which is why the clinical picture is usually a sensory neuropathy rather than generalized CNS toxicity.
edges.summary: This is one of the clearer supplement neurotoxicity edges. The strongest human signal comes from a large overdose case series and later pharmacovigilance data, both of which show that prolonged pyridoxine exposure can produce bilateral sensory neuropathic symptoms that often improve after withdrawal but are not always trivial.
edges.caveats: The older literature involves clearly supraphysiologic doses, while newer supplement-era reports raise the possibility that toxicity may emerge at lower doses in susceptible users. The evidence is not a reason to avoid physiologic replacement, but it is a reason not to normalize chronic megadose vitamin B6 use.
